articles.title: Erling Haaland haircut: Zlatan Ibrahimovic, Jack Grealish & Noel Gallagher shocked
articles.summary: Manchester City striker Erling Haaland reveals his new buzz cut on social media.
articles.body:
Whether it be Zlatan Ibrahimovic, Gareth Bale or Erling Haaland, football has witnessed some iconic man buns over the years.

However, Haaland has decided to begin the new Premier League season with a new - and very different - look.

The Manchester City striker revealed on social media that he had shed his famous blonde locks, posting the caption: "New season, new trim."

Haaland will be hoping his new look brings even more goals as he aims to get off the mark when Enzo Maresca's side face Bournemouth at 14:00 BST on Sunday.

Before cutting his hair, Haaland joked around by showing off some images of his previous hairstyles during his career, and some questionable ideas of how his new hair should look.

Looking nervous as the hairdresser cut the first piece, it didn't take long for Haaland to start smiling about his new appearance.

There were mixed reactions when the 26âyearâold made video calls to City team-mate Jack Grealish, Oasis' Noel Gallagher and former City manager Pep Guardiola.

Gallagher said: "You look about 17 years old. It's good. Change is good."

Grealish and Guardiola both said they "love" the change.

"You look about 10 years old. That is hilarious. I can't stop looking at the front of your hair. I love it," said Grealish.

"No way. You're lucky you have hair. I would love to have it. I love it," said Guardiola.

Before calling Ibrahimovic, Haaland joked that the former Sweden international told him never to cut his long hair.

"Zlatan told me, never cut your hair, because your strength is in your hair. I'm a bit nervous. I want a buzz cut, like in the military."

It turned out Ibrahimovic was not impressed that Haaland didn't follow his advice.

"What did you do? You lost a bet or what? Block me and erase my number," Ibrahimovic said.

articles.title: Eyed by Lane Kiffin, How Much More Money Could Jack Pyburn Get from LSU Compared to Bucs Contract?
articles.summary: For former LSU linebacker Jack Pyburn, getting cut by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ahead of the 2026 NFL season might be financially advantageous.
articles.body:
For former LSU linebacker Jack Pyburn, getting cut by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ahead of the 2026 NFL season might be financially advantageous.

Pyburn is among those who could head back to college after a Louisiana judge granted a restraining order in his favor.

"I'm kind of caught in the middle of a whirlwind, and I'm just trying to play football," he said, per The Athletic's Matt Baker .

Pyburn signed with the Buccaneers as an undrafted free agent. Should he make Tampa Bay's squad, he'd earn an $885,000 base salary for 2026. His three-year deal is worth $3.1 million overall.

According to Baker, two NIL agents pegged his value "in the $1 million range" if he were to play another year in college.

Because of the judge's order, coaches could potentially add new players less than two weeks out from the start of the regular season.

LSU's Lane Kiffin was an early adopter in terms of building his team through the transfer portal. In light of recent events, he's keeping his options open.

"There's a lot into that," he told reporters when asked of making late changes. "The questions that come to that. So, it's a fair question but I'm not going to comment on any of it. It's too many directions of questions that it could go to."

Pyburn made 41 appearances over four seasons, the first three coming with Florida before he headed for Baton Rouge. With the Tigers last year, he had two sacks and 5.5 tackles for loss.

Making the Buccaneers is probably the best thing for Pyburn's football career.

Maybe he could earn more in NIL money than the NFL minimum salary, but practicing against pros and possibly seeing meaningful snaps will help better develop his game.

Pyburn may now have a nice fallback in the event he doesn't crack the final 53-man roster.

articles.title: Diego Maradona 'Hand of God' Ball Sells for $3.4M at Auction, Used in 1986 FIFA World Cup
articles.summary: The Adidas Azteca ball Argentina legend Diego Maradona scored with twice during the 1986 World Cup quarterfinals against England—the famous "Hand of God" and "Goal of the Century" tallies—sold for $3.35 million at Heritage Auctions on Saturday night, per multiple reports.
articles.body:
The Adidas Azteca ball Argentina legend Diego Maradona scored with twice during the 1986 World Cup quarterfinals against England—the famous "Hand of God" and "Goal of the Century" tallies—sold for $3.35 million at Heritage Auctions on Saturday night, per multiple reports .

That was well below the $10 million estimates. Maradona's kit from that match had previously sold for $9.3 million.

Live All the Action: Fulham vs. Chelsea 🔥

"When it came in, I worked at Heritage for 20 years and there's been a lot of items that when they arrived, they just shut down the whole department. This is on that list," Heritage production manager Mike Provenzale told The Athletic's Larry Holder and Asli Pelit in July regarding the ball. "It's an item so iconic, even people who don't know anything about soccer or know the event can realize the value behind the ball. Having it photo matched to both goals is just the cherry on top."

articles.title: Jeremiah Smith's Dad Reacts to WR Being Named Ohio State Captain in Heartwarming Video
articles.summary: The best player in college football is going to be one of the captains of the top-ranked team in college football going into the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The best player in college football is going to be one of the captains of the top-ranked team in college football going into the 2026 season.

Ohio State announced its full list of seven captains for the upcoming campaign, and star wide receiver Jeremiah Smith was one of those selected by his teammates. The Buckeyes also released an emotional video of Smith and wide receivers coach Cortez Hankton calling the playmaker's father to break the news:

"I'm going to tell you how much it means to him," Hankton said in the video. "This young dude over here had tears of joy afterwards. Just when he was named and when he found out how much he means to his teammates. He walks around every day with a sense of humility and grace and does his job at a high level.

"But to be named the captain, it means a lot to him. I want you to know that. We're all proud of him."

Smith was joined by wide receiver Brandon Inniss, defensive end Kenyatta Jackson Jr., safety Jaylen McClain, linebacker Payton Pierce, quarterback Julian Sayin and offensive lineman Austin Siereveld as the team captains.

Smith stands out as the clear-cut best player in the sport, at least in the eyes of B/R's NFL Scouting Department. The wide receiver was ranked No. 1 on the early big board with a score of 9.8, creating plenty of separation from the 9.0 score for second-ranked player Leonard Moore.

In fact, the ninth-ranked player was closer to Moore than Moore was to Smith.

All the wide receiver has done in two years at Ohio State is win a national championship in his first and be named a consensus All-American in his second. He had more than 1,200 receiving yards in each season and has 27 career touchdown catches.

He has also been at his best in some of the biggest moments with a combined 290 yards and four touchdowns in College Football Playoff wins over Tennessee and Oregon, a touchdown in the national championship game win over Notre Dame, and touchdowns in each of his two games against archrival Michigan.

Expect more of the same from the potential Heisman contender in 2026, especially now that he is a captain of the Buckeyes.

articles.title: Newcastle 2-2 Liverpool: Relief for Andoni Iraola but Reds have work to do
articles.summary: Dominik Szoboszlai's injury-time penalty rescues a point at the start of the Andoni Iraola era - but Liverpool need to improve after below-par display.
articles.body:
When Liverpool came to Newcastle last August, there was utter jubilation as Rio Ngumoha scored a remarkable 100th-minute winner.

They scored late again this time around, through Dominik Szoboszlai's 99th-minute penalty, but it felt more like a sense of relief than joy as they rescued a point.

Andoni Iraola said afterwards that his side did not deserve to lose and, to their credit, they never gave up as they earned a 2-2 draw .

A defeat would have been Liverpool 's first on the opening weekend since 2012-13. A draw will do wonders for their spirit but it will certainly not mask their concerns.

"It's probably not the result you want when you come in before the game but we definitely deserve this point and even more," Iraola told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"The team has never given up and we've recovered one point and probably the taste is better because we score in the last minute."

Iraola will be content with the outcome, given his side trailed twice at a raucous St James' Park.

But on the flight back to Merseyside on Sunday evening, he would have had time to consider the performance, which highlighted why his squad needs more depth.

"You're expecting Liverpool to get top four this season at least but they didn't look like a top four team today," former Scotland winger Pat Nevin told 5 Live.

"There are more players to come in, so you can't make a real decision on how their season is going to go.

"There's a definite lack of creativity and somehow they must get the best out of Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak because you certainly didn't get the best out of them today."

All eyes were on Wirtz and Isak - the Sweden striker, signed from Newcastle in a drawn-out saga last September, was booed relentlessly whenever he touched the ball. Wirtz did start positively, but was replaced just after the hour mark after Newcastle went 2-1 up.

Isak had 28 touches and looked fired up but wasted a brilliant opportunity in the second half - the kind of which he would take regularly when he was at Newcastle .

Both of them, signed for nine-figure fees last summer, will know that their overall output and connection must improve over the coming weeks and months.

This remains a Liverpool side offering more questions than answers.

One significant question is the Cody Gakpo conundrum, which will roll into the final week of the transfer window.

If Liverpool do bring in two more attacking players then Gakpo may leave.

The club have been linked with Paris St-Germain's Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye and have had two bids rejected for Brighton 's Yankuba Minteh.

Yet Dutchman Gakpo was Liverpool 's best player at Newcastle and took his goal brilliantly - while there was another positive in the performance of Spanish forward Victor Munoz on his Liverpool debut from the bench.

Munoz won the late penalty after replacing Ngumoha but Iraola's decision to take off the English teenager off after just over an hour summed up how much he struggled down the right.

Ngumoha will turn 18 next week and has preferred to play down the left throughout his youth career but failed to have an impact on the other side.

With Iraola determined to have his wingers able to play on both sides, it remains to be seen if that experiment persists once Liverpool get more attackers in.

What is for certain is that Iraola needs more options. Once Munoz and Alexis Mac Allister came on in the 63rd minute, Iraola's remaining bench options were: Giorgi Mamardashvili, Ronald Araujo, Wataru Endo, Kostas Tsimikas, Trey Nyoni, James McConnell and Lewis Koumas.

Defensively, both Milos Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong had poor games at full-back and Liverpool were undone on the counter attack for both of the goals they conceded.

The lack of a defensive midfielder showed and it was revealing to see Iraola use Mac Allister just ahead of the back four after Joe Willock put Newcastle 2-1 up.

Liverpool have now conceded more goals via fast breaks in all competitions than any other Premier League team since the start of last season - nine.

All that and more will be food for thought for the new Liverpool boss but this was a relatively positive start to life under Iraola - who prefers to wait until the day after the match for a debrief.

"I've liked a lot of the things I've seen from the team," he said. "There's definitely things to improve like the goals but I've seen a lot of things I've liked from the team. I've liked the energy, especially the players coming from the bench. I think we finished the game quite strong physically."

"We will never give up. I can guarantee you that," Szoboszlai told Sky Sports. "We have to fight every time - all day long during the 90 minutes. Everybody who came off the bench also made an impact as well. We need the whole squad and we need to be ready."

That desire was never a cause for concern on Tyneside. But this Liverpool squad must improve, both in terms of quality and quantity.

articles.title: Oregon's Dan Lanning Takes Firm Stance on NFL Players Returning to CFB amid New LSU Commit
articles.summary: It's safe to say Oregon head coach Dan Lanning isn't going to be studying NFL rosters for potential additions.
articles.body:
It's safe to say Oregon head coach Dan Lanning isn't going to be studying NFL rosters for potential additions.

While ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Sunday that tight end Dae'Quan Wright will join LSU from the transfer portal if he clears waivers after the Cleveland Browns waived him, Lanning took a strong position against such a path back to college football.

"I think there are a lot of negatives that are involved around this," he told reporters. "One, once you go to the NFL, to me, you're in the NFL. You don't get the opportunity to come back. Two, most of us have built our rosters. You have a limited roster now.

"So if you've invited somebody back to your team, that means you're kicking somebody else off your team to match your roster limits. I don't think that's fair to players who worked all summer, all spring, and put themselves in position to be ready to work for a team."

As for Wright, Schefter noted he is "believed to be the first player who could play for an NFL team, and then go back to play in college."

The tight end went undrafted but signed with the Philadelphia Eagles and then joined the Browns via waivers on Aug. 11. He has not appeared in either of Cleveland's two preseason games.

ESPN reported he was among those college athletes who filed a lawsuit when they, as 2022 high school graduates, were not included in the NCAA's new rule allowing five years of eligibility for Division I athletes.

That rule doesn't take effect until next season.

Wright was granted a temporary restraining order in Louisiana, which maintained his eligibility to return to college.

While the NCAA received a stay Friday from the Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals that reversed a ruling from a federal judge "that had opened the door for all athletes who started college in the 2022-23 academic year and played for four consecutive seasons to return for a fifth season," it did not apply for athletes who successfully petitioned for restraining orders in state courts.

That Wright would go to LSU is not surprising considering he played for Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin at Ole Miss last season and helped lead the Rebels to the College Football Playoff.

As for Lanning, he has a CFP contender in Oregon even without the help of players who had already joined the NFL. The Ducks are No. 2 in the Associated Press Top 25 and open the season on Sept. 5 against Boise State.

articles.title: SC Cambuur fans suffer burns and eye injuries after Feyenoord supporters throw fireworks
articles.summary: Dutch side SC Cambuur says fans were left with "burns, hearing damage and eye injuries"  after Feyenoord supporters threw fireworks during Sunday's Eredivisie match.
articles.body:
Dutch club SC Cambuur said fans have suffered "burns, hearing damage and eye injuries" after Feyenoord supporters threw fireworks during Sunday's league match.

Play was suspended for around 10 minutes in the first half after visiting fans in the away end at the Kooi Stadion lit a large number of red flares and threw fireworks.

Some of the fireworks were aimed towards sections containing home fans and SC Cambuur said in a statement that five supporters were confirmed to have been injured.

Feyenoord said it "firmly distances itself from the unacceptable events" and that head coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst - an assistant to Arne Slot at Liverpool last season - apologised on behalf of the club to SC Cambuur after the match.

"It should be clear that setting off and firing fireworks is completely unacceptable and has no place in a football stadium whatsoever," SC Cambuur said.

The club, who were promoted to the Eredivisie last season after three seasons in the Dutch second tier, said it would work with the authorities to make sure those responsible were punished, while Feyenoord said they would request camera footage.

Last season, an Eredivisie match between Ajax and Groningen was abandoned after fireworks and flares were ignited behind one of the goals at Johan Cruyff Arena.

Feyenoord's general manager Robert Eenhoorn said he "cannot be happy" with their 5-2 victory in Leeuwarden, adding "frustration prevails too much for that".

"This problem obviously does not only affect Feyenoord and is unfortunately something we have been unable to put a stop to for decades," Eenhoorn said.

"We will therefore have to sit down again with all stakeholders, clubs, the KNVB [Dutch football association], and the authorities to look for a solution together."

Leeuwarden mayor Foort van Oosten also condemned the incident and promised an investigation, while the Dutch football association said it would revisit its protocols for incidents of disorder.

The game resumed despite the injuries to the fans, but it would have been abandoned had a player or match official been hit.

"That doesn't feel right," Jan Bluyssen, the KNVB's manager of professional football competition affairs, told Dutch news agency ANP.

"We need to examine whether the protocol is still appropriate and how we might want to adjust it."

articles.summary: The Carabao Cup is back for the 2026/27 season, with every second-round tie live on Sky Sports; watch Chelsea vs Luton, Tottenham vs Charlton, Fulham vs AFC Wimbledon, Newcastle vs West Brom, Preston vs Everton and more
articles.body:
The Carabao Cup is back for the 2026/27 season, with every second-round tie live on Sky Sports!

On Wednesday, you can see Newcastle hope to clinch a first win under Matthias Jaissle when West Brom visit St James' Park, while Tottenham look to bounce back from a 3-0 humbling at Brentford at home to early Championship pace-setters Charlton.

The same night, David Moyes will make his first return to Deepdale since leaving Preston in 2002 when he visits with Everton, before Chelsea host Luton and Fulham likewise with AFC Wimbledon in Thursday's double header.

The third round draw takes place live on Sky Sports following Preston's clash with Everton on Wednesday night. Fixtures take place across two weeks (weeks beginning 7 and 14 September), with 32 teams involved - 23 winners from round two and the nine Premier League clubs competing in UEFA competitions.

Additional draw conditions will be in place due to the expanded European competition calendar. articles.title: Julian Alvarez transfer news: Arsenal, Barcelona or Atletico Madrid stay for striker?
articles.summary: An analysis of Julian Alvarez's future with the transfer window closing on 1 September - and the Argentine's chances of a move from Atletico Madrid to Arsenal.
articles.body:
Acrimony, anger and animosity: the Julian Alvarez summer transfer saga in a nutshell.

The boos aimed at the Atletico Madrid forward from his own supporters at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday provided the latest twist in what has been one of the most bitter - and certainly public - storylines of the window.

And with deadline day on 1 September, the Argentine World Cup winner's future remains one of the hottest topics.

In simplistic terms the dispute comes down to this: Alvarez wants to join Barcelona - but Atletico won't let him.

The Madrid club's steadfast refusal to sanction the 26-year-old's dream move to the Spotify Camp Nou has led to one of the most rancorous public falling-outs in recent memory.

The feud led to Atleti fans jeering their own player on his return to club action after the summer World Cup in a 2-2 home draw with Villarreal on Sunday.

Atletico Madrid president Enrique Cerezo, speaking last week, said: "I don't know if he will say sorry, but Julian is an excellent person and I am absolutely sure that he will win over the fans in two games.

"I said he wouldn't be sold, he's our player and an important part of our team. We like that he's with us and think he will have a magnificent season."

Nevertheless, the events that unfolded on Sunday certainly haven't gone unnoticed at Arsenal .

BBC Sport has consistently reported over the summer that Alvarez is viewed as the Gunners' dream transfer target.

But for the vast majority of the window, Arsenal 's interest has been largely dormant because they were fully aware of his desire to join Barcelona.

They have been waiting for the right moment to strike and those at the Emirates are hopeful that time may be coming.

Gunners lying in wait and ready to move quickly

Arsenal are realistic about their chances of signing Alvarez before next week's transfer deadline.

Do they want him? Yes. Are they trying? Yes. Can they pull it off? The answer to that question is less unequivocal.

Manager Mikel Arteta and sporting director Andrea Berta know it is a long shot, not least because former Manchester City forward Alvarez, at least so far, has shown little indication he would be willing to join the club.

His current reluctance to give the green light on a move to London isn't necessarily linked to any apprehension towards Arsenal - but rather that doing so would see him forgoing his dream of joining Barcelona.

Alvarez has also been made aware of certain visa regulations that would create difficulty for his family visiting him in the UK.

Moving to Catalonia is what he truly wants.

What's more, the Camp Nou club are absolutely willing to make that happen.

But Atleti are absolutely adamant they will not sell Alvarez to Barcelona.

In May, they made a series of social media posts brutally mocking the pursuit by the Spanish champions of their player to millions of followers.

"Don't believe everything you see, especially if it's related to Barca," Atletico posted. "In recent months, we've been suffering a smear campaign against one of our players."

For the Madrid side, the matter is closed and that leaves Alvarez's dream in serious jeopardy.

Therein lies a sliver of hope for Arsenal because, as things stand, the only way out is a move to the Emirates Stadium.

Indeed, according to well-placed sources there has been a slight softening of Alvarez's stance in recent days, although not enough yet to get anyone at Arsenal excited.

But should he change his mind in the final days of the window, then the Gunners are poised.

Since the start of the summer, according to BBC Sport sources, Arsenal have been confident Alvarez's move to Barcelona was a non-starter.

But while he still harboured hope of fulfilling that ambition, Arteta's men focused on the captures of Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa, while also trying to bring Real Madrid attacker Vinicius Jr to London.

With the Brazilian extending his contract to stay in Spain, Arsenal have now decided to step things up regarding Alvarez.

Atleti director Mateu Alemany was in London last week, where he is understood to have met with Arsenal counterparts - and made clear his side would seek a fee of 150m euros (Â£128m).

The Gunners are confident they can finance any deal and quickly finalise the transfer - if he said yes.

Arteta is fully aware if Alvarez was to join Arsenal this summer he would only be doing so because his preferred destination was not possible.

It is understood the Spaniard is comfortable with that scenario and believes Alvarez would eventually become fully invested and committed to the Arsenal project.

The ball is now in Alvarez's court. If he wants to leave Atletico, which sources close to the attacker insist that he does, then the Premier League champions appear to be his only option.

Alvarez joined Atletico for Â£81m from Manchester City in August 2024 , having spent just over two years at the Etihad following a Â£14.1m move from Argentine side River Plate.

He won six major trophies at City - including the Treble of Premier League, FA Cup and Champions League in 2023 - scoring 36 goals in 106 appearances.

At Atletico, he has scored 49 goals in 107 appearances, but has not yet won any silverware.

Could Alvarez also concede defeat in his efforts to leave Atleti this summer and attempt to mend what appears to be a broken relationship with the club and its supporters?

It is possible, although, according to those close to the player, it is his belief that the Madrid club are being unreasonable. Indeed the player's agent Fernando Hidalgo has been open with his disdain towards how his client has been treated this summer.

That said, Alvarez is described as a private individual and said to be deeply uncomfortable about the very public nature of the conflict with his club - although the player himself also outlined his desire to leave publicly during the World Cup.

"A transfer is the best option," he said.

When Real Madrid released a statement on 9 June saying they had an offer of 150m euros (Â£128m) rejected by their neighbours, there was a sense from the Alvarez camp Atletico had reneged on an agreement to let the striker leave if they received an offer of that amount.

Of course, the prospect of selling Alvarez to their fiercest rivals was viewed as a non-starter by Atletico.

For South Americans - playing for Real or Barca represents the holy grail.

Hansi Flick's side remain interested in Alvarez, but fear Atletico's stance isn't purely posturing and have started to consider alternative options, including Arsenal 's Swedish striker Viktor Gyokeres.

If they decide to turn their attention elsewhere, Alvarez will have a decision to make.

Arsenal or nothing? We'll have the answer soon.

articles.title: Liverpool: Florian Wirtz part of potentially a worst-ever transfer window, says Jamie Carragher as Reds' midfield problems exposed
articles.summary: Liverpool drew their opening Premier League fixture 2-2 at Newcastle on Sunday but Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher explained on Monday Night Football why the Reds' midfield set-up - and lack of impact from Florian Wirtz - is a big problem for new boss Andoni Iraola.
articles.body:
Jamie Carragher says he doesn't see where Florian Wirtz fits into the Liverpool team - and the £116.5m German could be part of the worst transfer window in Premier League history.

During a damning assessment of the Reds' midfield set-up in their 2-2 draw at Newcastle, Carragher also explained the big weakness in new boss Andoni Iraola's tactical approach at Liverpool and why it will prevent them from launching a Premier League title challenge this season.

Here's how the Sky Sports pundit broke down Liverpool's big issues on Monday Night Football...

A midfield dilemma

"I don't believe that midfield can function with the personnel in there," said Carragher. "For me, it doesn't work. And it's not just about personnel, it's the structure the manager is asking."

Liverpool fielded Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai in midfield at St James' Park, with Florian Wirtz at No 10.

However, rather than sitting in a double pivot, Szoboszlai often moved forward into more attacking areas.

Carragher noted how Man City have had success in the past with a double-pivot and No 10 set-up but added: "Why did [Pep] Guardiola always bring his full-backs inside? Because the holding midfield player needed help to stop counter-attacks. Straight away that's a problem for me [with Liverpool].

Carragher showed examples of not only Szoboszlai but also Gravenberch charging forwards to join Wirtz and emptying the midfield - providing space for Newcastle to counter-attack into.

"All they think about is going forwards. All three of them. And that's why it can't work," said Carragher.

"I don't think I've ever seen a more offensive team, or players who think offensively in the Premier League than that. There's only the two centre-backs who don't think about going forward."

Carragher also noted how it appears to be an instruction from Iraola for Wirtz and Szoboszlai to 'lock on' to opposition midfielders.

However, while Brentford had success employing a similarly aggressive tactic against Tottenham because their centre-backs stepped up to close the space behind, Liverpool's Virgil van Dijk didn't make the same move. Instead, the 35-year-old centre-back sat deeper.

"You've got a situation, like at Man Utd under Erik ten Hag a few years ago - a team who want to press high but with a deep block.

"That's why these big holes are appearing. The midfield players want to lock on and Van Dijk does not want to come with them."

On Van Dijk, Carragher added: "He needs protecting, he needs cuddling, he needs looking after."

  • Transfer Centre LIVE! | Liverpool news & transfers🔴
  • Liverpool fixtures & scores | FREE Liverpool highlights▶️
  • Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺

Holding midfield signing essential

After watching Liverpool against Newcastle, Carragher says it is now essential they sign a holding midfielder to offer them more security against fast breaks.

"Liverpool need someone alongside Gravenberch," said Carragher. "It doesn't necessarily need to be a player who can't get on the ball and he's just tackling and stopping players. If you play for one of the top teams in the world, you need to be able to get hold of the ball. But I want someone who can run.

"Szboszlai has to go to the No 10."

What to do with Wirtz?

If a holding midfielder comes in alongside Gravenberch and Szoboszlai goes to No 10, where does Wirtz go?

Carragher doesn't see a suitable role for him in the Liverpool team with Iraola's set-up.

He says the German's lack of end product with Liverpool - just five goals and three assists in 33 Premier League appearances last season - means it is fair to question whether he will ever be the answer.

"This thing that it takes people a year to settle in the Premier League, I think is a bit of a myth. I don't think there's too many examples where it does," said Carragher.

"I've always seen this coming. When people are saying [Wirtz] has got to go to No 10, that means Szoboszlai's got to be in the team and he's not a central midfield player.

"I thought this would come up in six weeks, I think it's coming up right now. I don't see where he fits in at all, really.

"What's Iraola going to do with Wirtz? You can't keep going with it, it's not working,

"It didn't work last season. Liverpool last season conceded 78 goals, 53 in the Premier League, the most they've ever conceded in the Premier League. And all of a sudden it's all about buying wingers?

"I'm not sure where he fits. I almost thought you could put him in a pocket from the left, where he plays for Germany, but Iraola loves wingers, he wants players who've got energy up and down the flank.

"I don't think we're seeing a massive underperformance. I think what we've seen for a year is probably what he is, which is a neat and tidy footballer. Not a player who should be worth £110m, someone who probably should be £50m-60m, something like that. Neat and tidy, lovely touch. I'm not sure what people are expecting."

Worst transfer window in Premier League history?

Wirtz was part of an enormous £445m transfer spend by Liverpool last summer, when it appeared they were out to supercharge Arne Slot's Premier League title-winning squad. Instead it went badly wrong, with Liverpool limping home in fifth, with Slot sacked.

As well as Wirtz, Liverpool also signed Alexander Isak for a Premier League record £125m, Hugo Ekitike (£79m), Milos Kerkez (£40m), Jeremie Frimpong (£29.5m), Giorgi Mamardashvili (£29m) and Giovanni Leoni (£26m).

Carragher reckons that transfer window may have hurt Liverpool more than it helped them. In fact, he reckons it could go down as the worst summer of business by a Premier League club ever.

"My fear is this window of 12 months ago could set Liverpool back a year or two to fix it," he said.

"Don't forget, last season it was not about these players. Because it was all about Arne Slot and his style of playing, and he's not like Jurgen Klopp, and he's holding his players back...

"But we're talking 12 months of under-performance from all of these players except Ekitike.

"If this doesn't change in the next two or three months, under Iraola, and these players improve, I think we're going to be looking at that as arguably the worst transfer window we've probably seen in Premier League history.

"When you consider the fees for these players, and what it was going to do for Liverpool... The idea wasn't for these players coming in just to be good players, it was to create something like a little dynasty for Liverpool.

"Let's not forget, Liverpool won the league two years ago. These were supposed to do what City have done in the last few years, or Manchester United in the past, where they've gone and won two or three leagues in five years."

Title contenders? Not this year...

With all that in mind, Carragher has little hope of his former club mounting a serious title challenge this season.

"I don't think Liverpool will be contenders this season," he said. "Liverpool are in transition

"I'm not trying to make excuses for them, because they've lost [Mohamed] Salah, Van Dijk is probably going to go, maybe this is his last season, and the goalkeeper Alisson. You're talking about three all-time greats there for Liverpool.

"So they're probably not going to be there in 12 months and these [signings of summer 2025] have got to find their feet, and Iraola has got to find his feet at a big club.

"For me, if Liverpool qualify for the Champions League this season, I'd be happy. The manager sort of beds in and then you can maybe go from there and look to challenge."
paragraphs:
Jamie Carragher says he doesn't see where Florian Wirtz fits into the Liverpool team - and the £116.5m German could be part of the worst transfer window in Premier League history.

During a damning assessment of the Reds' midfield set-up in their 2-2 draw at Newcastle, Carragher also explained the big weakness in new boss Andoni Iraola's tactical approach at Liverpool and why it will prevent them from launching a Premier League title challenge this season.

Here's how the Sky Sports pundit broke down Liverpool's big issues on Monday Night Football...

A midfield dilemma

"I don't believe that midfield can function with the personnel in there," said Carragher. "For me, it doesn't work. And it's not just about personnel, it's the structure the manager is asking."

Liverpool fielded Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai in midfield at St James' Park, with Florian Wirtz at No 10.

However, rather than sitting in a double pivot, Szoboszlai often moved forward into more attacking areas.

Carragher noted how Man City have had success in the past with a double-pivot and No 10 set-up but added: "Why did [Pep] Guardiola always bring his full-backs inside? Because the holding midfield player needed help to stop counter-attacks. Straight away that's a problem for me [with Liverpool].

Carragher showed examples of not only Szoboszlai but also Gravenberch charging forwards to join Wirtz and emptying the midfield - providing space for Newcastle to counter-attack into.

"All they think about is going forwards. All three of them. And that's why it can't work," said Carragher.

"I don't think I've ever seen a more offensive team, or players who think offensively in the Premier League than that. There's only the two centre-backs who don't think about going forward."

Carragher also noted how it appears to be an instruction from Iraola for Wirtz and Szoboszlai to 'lock on' to opposition midfielders.

However, while Brentford had success employing a similarly aggressive tactic against Tottenham because their centre-backs stepped up to close the space behind, Liverpool's Virgil van Dijk didn't make the same move. Instead, the 35-year-old centre-back sat deeper.

"You've got a situation, like at Man Utd under Erik ten Hag a few years ago - a team who want to press high but with a deep block.

"That's why these big holes are appearing. The midfield players want to lock on and Van Dijk does not want to come with them."

On Van Dijk, Carragher added: "He needs protecting, he needs cuddling, he needs looking after."

articles.title: Deion Sanders Says Subpoena in Son Shilo's Bankruptcy Case Not a Distraction Ahead of Season Opener
articles.summary: BOULDER, Colo. (AP) — Deion Sanders has a knack for staying in the headlines whether it's on the field or in court proceedings.
articles.body:
BOULDER, Colo. (AP) — Deion Sanders has a knack for staying in the headlines whether it's on the field or in court proceedings.

The Colorado football coach recently had a sheriff's deputy show up on campus in an attempt to serve him civil papers as part of a bankruptcy trial involving his son, Shilo. Several days later, his lawyer filed a motion to dismiss the case involving some logos the coach uses on boxer briefs, cowboy hats and other things he sells on his website.

The legal wrangling comes with the clock ticking toward Colorado's season opener at Georgia Tech on Sept. 3.

Sanders bristled at the notion any of it was a distraction for a team that has become familiar with them since bringing on a celebrity coach.

"Do you think that's my first subpoena?" Sanders said Monday regarding the Boulder County Sheriff's Office attempt to deliver a subpoena on Aug. 11 in the case involving his son. "When you have 'it,' when you're 'him,' you get sued. You have off-the-field foolishness that if someone really sat down and explained it to you, you would say, 'You've got to be kidding. But it is what it is.

"I don't know anyone that's a game-changer, a way-maker, that is not dealing with some type of lawsuit."

Shilo Sanders' bankruptcy case stems from an incident with a security guard when he was in high school. The guard filed a lawsuit against Sanders and was issued a default judgment when Sanders didn't show for his court date. The original suit said the guard sustained permanent injuries.

"You know Shilo won this is case previously, right? Anybody know that?" Sanders said Monday as he kicks off his fourth season at Colorado on the heels of a 3-9 campaign. "Raise your hand if you knew that. That Shilo got awarded money for this. OK. Check it out.

"I can't wait until it's over and he gets to tell his story. He already won this case."

Deion Sanders faces a separate and unrelated lawsuit in U.S. District Court in Nebraska involving the use of logos. The suit was filed more than a year ago by the man who designed them, Alan Tipp.

Created as part of an Under Armour sunglasses deal, it didn't succeed commercially, according to the court filing by Sanders' attorney last Friday. After Sanders' deal with the apparel company expired, the company allowed him to keep the logos. In the motion to dismiss filed by Sanders' attorney it said the designer "messaged Sanders over the course of several years to express gratitude that the logos were still being used.

"Nevertheless, after lying in wait for close to a decade, on January 30, 2025, Tipp filed this action against Sanders, his merchandising company Prime Time Enterprises, Inc., and his management company, SMAC Entertainment, LLC, claiming he is owed millions of dollars in damages for the supposed unauthorized use of 'his' work."

articles.title: Valencia - Betis | Segunda prueba de nivel de hastío en Mestalla: previa, análisis, pronóstico y predicción
articles.standfirst: La grada estalló al final del primer partido de Liga ante el Celta (0-0) contra el técnico y los jugadores
articles.summary: La grada estalló al final del primer partido de Liga ante el Celta (0-0) contra el técnico y los jugadores
articles.body: Parece exagerado plantear la segunda jornada de Liga como un ejercicio para templar los nervios de una afición. Pero el final del partido contra el Celta se convirtió en una nueva escalada de reproches de la grada del Valencia contra su entrenador, Carlos Corberán, y también contra los futbolistas. Mestalla esperó al pitido final para recuperar sensaciones y reacciones que recuerdan al hastío que se arrastra desde la temporada pasada. El Betis, además, es un rival Champions que arrancó el curso con victoria. Con el ambiente enrarecido tras el empate frente al Celta, aunque con la convicción por parte del entrenador de que los cinco defensas pueden ser una buena opción para construir una base que no sea solo circunstancial. La baja de Justin de Haas permitirá que Diakhaby entre en el once titular y las dudas vienen por la escasa producción ofensiva que mostró el equipo hace tres días. Si el entrenador insiste en Danjuma, podría acompañarlo de Hugo Duro por probar una combinación diferente que pueda aumentar el número de ocasiones. Los tres puntos logrados el pasado viernes en el estreno liguero ante la Real Sociedad, un rival directo, permiten al Betis llegar a Mestalla repleto de confianza y sumando refuerzos a su expedición: el irlandés Troy Parrott, última incorporación al plantel, viajó con el equipo y podría tener sus primeros minutos como verdiblanco. Pellegrini sigue sin poder contar por diferentes problemas físicos con Diego Conde, Ruibal, Lo Celso, Abde, Morante y Petit, al tiempo que espera un final de mercado que, independientemente de lo que ocurra con Dani Ceballos, un nombre más vinculado a los deseos del club que del propio técnico, le traiga un pivote defensivo con la figura del marroquí Amrabat como prioridad absoluta. Hasta entonces, intentará seguir su buena dinámica en sus visitas a Mestalla, donde suma cuatro triunfos y un empate en sus seis últimas visitas.

articles.title: Jenni Hermoso, sobre su fichaje por el Atleti: "Mi futuro puede estar cerca de casa"
articles.standfirst: "A nivel físico y mental quiero seguir disfrutando esto que he hecho toda mi vida y que tanto me ha hecho feliz", comenta la futbolista
articles.summary: "A nivel físico y mental quiero seguir disfrutando esto que he hecho toda mi vida y que tanto me ha hecho feliz", comenta la futbolista
articles.body: Jenni Hermoso, campeona del mundo con España, dijo este lunes que a sus 36 años aún no se plantea dejar el fútbol, cuya carrera continuará en Europa. "Ni pienso en el retiro. No he pensado en ese primer paso para que decir: 'Ya no puedo más'. A nivel físico y mental quiero seguir disfrutando esto que he hecho toda mi vida y que tanto me ha hecho feliz. Me he sentido muy feliz en México, quiero continuar disfrutando del fútbol que es mi vida y colgar las botas hasta que diga que ya no puedo más", afirmó la delantera. Hermoso, quien el pasado 16 de agosto se despidió del club Tigres, mantuvo el suspense sobre su nuevo destino. "Hoy sigo pensando en el terreno de juego. Mi futuro puede estar cerca de casa, es todo lo que puedo decir", subrayó. Hermoso llegó al fútbol mexicano en el torneo de Apertura 2022 para jugar con el Pachuca, conjunto con el que participó en 41 partidos y anotó 26 goles. Firmó con Tigres para el Clausura 2024, equipo con el que jugó 44 partidos, marcó 10 goles y conquistó un título de liga y uno de campeón de campeonas. La delantera dejó ver su nostalgia por todo lo que vivió en este país. "Dejar todo esto en Monterrey, en México, no fue fácil. Me permitieron echar raíces aquí. Creo que dejo un pequeño regalo en esta ciudad. Llegué con el sueño de ser campeona y lo conseguí, por eso ahora debo ir en busca de nuevos retos que me permitirán mantenerme ilusionada para seguir jugando fútbol al más alto nivel", apuntó. "Pienso que la vida se compone de ciclos. Este es un momento adecuado para cambiar, recargarme y aunque México lo siento como mi casa, los cambios son atrevidos y siempre son necesarios", agregó. Hermoso, quien inició su carrera en el Atlético de Madrid, compartió su orgullo por haber ayudado al crecimiento y difusión de la liga femenina del fútbol mexicano, que data de 2017. "La liga en México tiene muchas cosas buenas, pero hay muchas cosas aún que debe mejorar para seguir creciendo. Una de ellas es seguir cuidando a las jugadoras. No sé si volveré mañana, pero me voy satisfecha sabiendo que puse un granito de arena para que se conociera más la liga mexicana", concluyó. Hermoso participó en la inauguración de una cancha de fútbol de una casa hogar para niñas en Monterrey, en el norte de México.

articles.title: Ferguson? Guardiola? Mourinho? Ranking the best managers in Premier League history
articles.summary: Thirteen managers have won the Premier League title, but which of them will make it into our top 10 covering the competition's history?
articles.body:
When it comes to ranking managers, titles are a good place to start.

Only four bosses have won more than one since the Premier League era began in 1992. So if you do some quick maths, you'll probably not be surprised by the names that top this list.

But there is a debate to be had around where they should rank, and who else makes it into the top 10. So let's have it.

You can rank your greatest managers of the Premier League era below too.

Longevity deserves a mention here. Take David Moyes, for example, racking up 755 games in Premier League dugouts - only Arsene Wenger (828) and Sir Alex Ferguson (810) have more.

Naturally, Moyes has the third-most wins in Premier League history too, although his 291 across spells with Everton, Manchester United, Sunderland and West Ham fall some way short of Wenger's 476 at Arsenal and Ferguson's 528 at United.

Pep Guardiola is also on Scotsman Moyes' shoulder despite managing barely half as many games.

Harry Redknapp has the fourth-most games under his belt (641), fifth-most wins (236) and also completes the top five for goals scored (818).

We should talk about win percentage too, and the former Tottenham manager who really deserves a shout here is Mauricio Pochettino, who guided Spurs to their best-ever Premier League finish of second in 2016-17 and also coached Southampton and Chelsea.

The Argentine is the only manager - of those who have coached more than 100 games - to have not lifted the title yet still won more than half his games throughout his Premier League career.

But really, to make this list, you have to have won a Premier League title. In total, 13 managers have done so. Meaning three are getting left at the door.

Arne Slot of Liverpool is the first to be cut. The others are a hard choice.

Manuel Pellegrini's Manchester City record was impressive before the Chilean made way for Guardiola. During those three years, plus 17 months at West Ham, his average of 1.92 goals per game ranks fifth among all managers with a century of matches.

But he spent big at the Hammers only to then endure a desperate run of form - so the man known as the Engineer, the only manager from outside Europe to win the title, misses out.

As does Antonio Conte, who had boom and bust spells at Chelsea and Spurs.

Instead, the pair are pipped by the only boss to win the title in all of Europe's top five leagues.

10. Carlo Ancelotti. Title winner 2009-10

AC Milan, Bayern Munich, Paris St-Germain, Real Madrid and, of course, Chelsea.

King Carlo has steered them all to domestic glory, not to mention his Champions League record of five successes. Yet his initial tenure in the English top flight was fleeting.

The Italian blitzed his way to the Premier League crown at the first time of asking at Stamford Bridge. But, after snapping up Fernando Torres for a then-British record fee from Liverpool the following January, Ancelotti was swiftly shown the door after Chelsea finished as runners-up in his second season.

A surprising return to England came via the Everton dugout, where Ancelotti delivered successive mid-table finishes before Real Madrid came calling.

Earlier this year, Mikel Arteta became the 13th manager to win the Premier League but the first Arsenal boss to do so since Arsene Wenger in 2004.

The Spaniard also snapped an eight-year run of either Manchester City or Liverpool winning the trophy.

Bursting clear of his rivals like they were a technical area, Arteta shrugged off questions over his team's sometimes robust style as well as those who suggested the Gunners were destined to always be runners-up.

As the only current Premier League boss to have won the title, and with Arsenal adding to an already stacked squad this summer, you wouldn't bet against the former playmaker creeping further up this list in future.

8. Roberto Mancini. Title winner 2011-12

Premier League titles don't come more dramatic than two goals in added time - including a 94th-minute winner - on the final day of the season, especially to clinch a first top-flight crown in more than 40 years while denying your arch-rivals.

Roberto Mancini got Manchester City's lavish new era rolling by winning the FA Cup in his first full season, having replaced Mark Hughes in December 2009, and followed up with the title before he was sacked the following summer.

The Italian, though, stacks up well, boasting the fourth-best points-per-game tally for any boss to have managed at least 100 Premier League games - coming in just above Conte and Jose Mourinho - and the fifth-best win percentage.

Meanwhile, his City stars make the top five for goals per game and boast the best record for fewest goals conceded, a miserly 0.83 per game.

Kenny Dalglish's greatest success as a boss came at Liverpool before the Premier League era began, winning three titles in four seasons, initially as a player-manager, before he departed in February 1991 after almost 15 years with the club.

He wound up at second-tier Blackburn Rovers eight months later and immediately steered them into the Premier League via the play-offs.

Bankrolled by local businessman Jack Walker, Rovers snapped up Alan Shearer from Southampton for a British record fee of Â£3.6m and then finished fourth and second before overcoming Manchester United to win the title in 1995.

That made Dalglish only the fourth manager to win the English top flight with two different clubs.

Dalglish was unable to repeat the trick at Newcastle, although they finished runners-up in both the league and FA Cup during his tenure, while his return to Liverpool ended in 2012 after League Cup success but an eighth-placed finish.

6. Claudio Ranieri. Title winner 2015-16

Dilly ding, dilly dong. Ranieri rides into the top six on pure vibes. The man behind the 5,000-1 miracle. The one who turned a cast of footballing misfits into an all-conquering force. The father of Leicester City's Premier League triumph.

That is worth his entry alone. Yet, in what seems another lifetime, the Tinkerman almost got his hands on a winner's medal more than a decade earlier.

Buoyed by the first wave of Roman Abramovich spending, Ranieri steered Chelsea to second in 2004, only behind Arsenal's Invincibles.

Chelsea probably should have won the Champions League too, losing in the semi-finals to Monaco, but that became a defining moment for the man who would replace him.

Jurgen Klopp is in some ways the Andy Murray of the Premier League. All action, high-octane performances, adored by his fans yet prickly under pressure. He enjoyed incredible success but would probably have dominated more were it not for a generational opponent.

In this rather stretched analogy, Manchester City are Klopp's Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic. If it had not been for his Catalan counterpart down the M62, Klopp's rock 'n' roll Reds would have been the undoubted top dogs under the German.

Instead, they racked up more than 90 points on three occasions and 'only' clinched one title in 2019-20 - it was, however, Liverpool's first in 30 years and their first of the Premier League era.

4. Jose Mourinho. Title winner 2004-05, 05-06 & 14-15

Lungs still pumping from that touchline sprint at Old Trafford, Jose Mourinho landed at Chelsea days after guiding Porto to a remarkable Champions League triumph and declared himself a 'Special One'.

Taking the baton from Ranieri and armed with a host of new signings, the Portuguese enigma stormed the title in his first season - Chelsea winning the league by 12 points, conceding only 15 goals and ruffling the raincoats of Wenger and Ferguson.

Mourinho backed it up in his second season before relationships began to fray and the most successful boss in the club's history left in September 2007. Mourinho, though, had transformed the Blues into a formidable force.

He returned six years later, after titles in Milan and Madrid, and clinched his third Premier League crown in his second season, only to be gone by Christmas of the following campaign.

Box-office spells followed at Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur, but they came nowhere near the success of his time in south-west London.

3. Arsene Wenger. Title winner 1997-98, 2001-02 & 03-04

It's fine margins between Wenger and Mourinho, as both their arrivals brought the dawn of new eras in the Premier League.

Indeed, Mourinho once said Wenger is a "specialist in failure", but in this list the Frenchman just pips his rival thanks to engineering the only 'Invincibles' season in Premier League history.

Wenger, joining from Japanese outfit Nagoya Grampus Eight, was deemed a curious choice at first but professionalised Arsenal and led them to league titles in 1998, 2002 and - the piece de resistance - that unbeaten season of 2003-04.

That he was unable to win another title in the 14 years that followed perhaps tarnishes Wenger's legacy slightly, but the Arsenal team he built during his first decade was one of the best the Premier League ever witnessed.

2. Pep Guardiola. Title winner 2017-18, 18-19, 20-21, 21-22, 22-23 & 23-24

Talking of managers who changed the face of English football, no-one has moved the game right from the elite level through to grassroots as much as Pep Guardiola.

Blame the Catalan for Sunday League goalkeepers playing out from the back.

And to think there were question marks over whether Guardiola's style - honed at Barcelona - would work in the more robust English game.

Guardiola was, of course, lavishly backed in the transfer market, but his Manchester City side won titles at a prolific rate.

City became the first English men's side to win four in a row - they landed six Premier League titles in total during Pep's decade in charge, as well as notching a century of points in 2018.

1. Sir Alex Ferguson. Title winner 1992-93, 93-94, 95-96, 96-97, 98-99, 99-2000, 2000-01, 02-03, 06-07, 07-08, 08-09, 10-11, 12-13

The first two decades of the Premier League were dominated by one man.

Sir Alex Ferguson won 13 titles and was able to continuously rebuild his side in order to keep Manchester United at the top of English football - from Eric Cantona to the '99 Treble winners, and later that front three of Cristiano Ronaldo, Wayne Rooney and Carlos Tevez.

Even after Ronaldo left for Real Madrid in 2009, and Tevez defected to the other side of Manchester, Ferguson continued winning titles until he retired in 2013.

His record title haul is more than double any manager from any era of men's English top-flight football, not just the Premier League - Guardiola, Liverpool's Bob Paisley and George Ramsay for Aston Villa are next on the list on six.

It makes Fergie the undoubted number one.

Only four bosses have won more than one since the Premier League era began in 1992. So if you do some quick maths, you'll probably not be surprised by the names that top this list.
But there is a debate to be had around where they should rank, and who else makes it into the top 10. So let's have it.
You can rank your greatest managers of the Premier League era below too.
Longevity deserves a mention here. Take David Moyes, for example, racking up 755 games in Premier League dugouts - only Arsene Wenger (828) and Sir Alex Ferguson (810) have more.

Naturally, Moyes has the third-most wins in Premier League history too, although his 291 across spells with Everton, Manchester United, Sunderland and West Ham fall some way short of Wenger's 476 at Arsenal and Ferguson's 528 at United.
Pep Guardiola is also on Scotsman Moyes' shoulder despite managing barely half as many games.

As does Antonio Conte, who had boom and bust spells at Chelsea and Spurs.
Instead, the pair are pipped by the only boss to win the title in all of Europe's top five leagues.
10. Carlo Ancelotti. Title winner 2009-10
AC Milan, Bayern Munich, Paris St-Germain, Real Madrid and, of course, Chelsea.

Earlier this year, Mikel Arteta became the 13th manager to win the Premier League but the first Arsenal boss to do so since Arsene Wenger in 2004.
The Spaniard also snapped an eight-year run of either Manchester City or Liverpool winning the trophy.

articles.title: Benítez, sobre la salida de Alonso del Madrid: "Tuvo similitudes conmigo, a Xabi le gustaba trabajar, organizar... pero en ese club hay mucha política"
articles.summary: Rafa Benítez valoró la salida de Xabi Alonso del Real Madrid en BBC Sports. El ex técnico madridista lo hizo en la previa del Fulham-Chelsea, encuentro en el que el tolosarra se media a Arbeloa. "En el Madrid, como dices, Xabi tiene muchas similitudes conmigo. A Alonso le gusta trabajar, organizar las cosas y después hablar con los jugadores sobre lo que quieren hacer. Pero en el Real Madrid hay mucha política alrededor. Así que quizá por eso fue más complicado", aseguró Benítez.

articles.title: Tchouaméni siembra la duda
articles.standfirst: El francés no se entrenó en la sesión previa al partido contra la Real Sociedad y apunta a baja para el duelo
articles.summary: El francés no se entrenó en la sesión previa al partido contra la Real Sociedad
articles.body: Vuelve la incógnita sobre Tchouaméni. El francés no se ha ejercitado hoy junto a sus compañeros en la previa del partido ante la Real Sociedad, que será el debut del conjunto blanco en el Santiago Bernabéu esta temporada. Tchouaméni ya superó unas molestias la semana pasada, algo que le permitió ejercitarse con el grupo antes del estreno liguero ante el Espanyol. Sin embargo, Mourinho consideró que todavía no estaba en las condiciones óptimas y el galo se quedó en Madrid. Tras una vuelta al trabajo en la que ayer sí trabajó junto al resto de sus compañeros, su ausencia de hoy parece dejar claro que todavía no está listo para jugar esta temporada y todo apunta a que volverá a caerse de la lista de convocados para medirse a la Real Sociedad. Tchouaméni no es el único con el que Mourinho no puede contar. Endrick, Militao, Mendy, Thiago, Rodrygo y Asencio siguen trabajando en sus respectivos procesos de recuperación y tampoco se les espera para el siguiente compromiso liguero.

articles.title: Transfer window 2026: What does your Premier League club need with a week to go?
articles.summary: BBC Sport takes a look at what each of the Premier League clubs still need before the summer transfer window shuts in seven days.
articles.body:
The first weekend of the Premier League season is complete but clubs still have one week of the transfer window remaining to secure last-minute squad additions.

Results are one thing but for many managers and sporting directors their opening match was an eye-opener in what positions need to be strengthened, who is no longer needed and what gaps still need to be plugged.

With the transfer window closing on Tuesday, 1 September at 23:00 BST, BBC Sport takes a look at what each top-flight club still needs and fans also have their say.

The Premier League champions have already strengthened the middle of the pitch with Bruno Guimaraes, the wing with Christos Tzolis and their defence with Ezri Konsa.

But Arsenal are still in the market for a forward and have a long-standing interest in Julian Alvarez.

Although it appears to be a difficult deal due to many factors, the Gunners will be ready to act if there is a chance to get it done.

If you want someone who is Premier League proven, who has won it all from the World Cup to the Champions League, Julian Alvarez looks like the guy that can take Arsenal to the promised land of finally getting over the line in Europe. Especially when there aren't that many elite forwards in the world.

Alvarez's Arsenal dilemma amid summer's most bitter transfer tussle Published 1 day ago

Alvarez's Arsenal dilemma amid summer's most bitter transfer tussle

Al-Hilal open talks to sign Arsenal winger Martinelli Published 1 day ago

Al-Hilal open talks to sign Arsenal winger Martinelli

What don't Aston Villa need after a raft of star departures this summer?

Ollie Watkins' transfer saga, with Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal trying to sign the striker, leaves Villa looking for a likely replacement with Nicolas Jackson a target.

A winger is also on the agenda while they need a defender after Ezri Konsa's move to Arsenal , and have opened talks for Club Brugge central defender Joel Ordonez after bids for Southampton centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis were rejected.

It is clear Aston Villa desperately require a striker more than anything right now.

Although I massively rate Victor Lindelof and Pau Torres, the display against Brighton has worried me slightly.

Therefore, I would welcome another centre-back as well.

It looks like we will be OK in midfield once Johan Manzambi is fit and with the addition of Leon Goretzka.

Watkins' departure would cut deepest - and Villa did not see it coming Published 1 day ago

Watkins' departure would cut deepest - and Villa did not see it coming

Villa in talks with Club Brugge for defender Ordonez Published 1 day ago

Villa in talks with Club Brugge for defender Ordonez

Bournemouth are used to being picked off and will simply be hoping to come through the final eight days of the transfer window unscathed.

It is clear that big clubs are circling for forward Eli Junior Kroupi and midfielder Alex Scott, who the Cherries insist are not for sale.

In terms of incomings, Bournemouth are largely done as they close in on a move for Juventus goalkeeper Michele Di Gregorio.

Brentford are in the fortunate position of being able to choose their deals carefully after some excellent squad strengthening.

The Bees have been looking at left-back, with West Ham's El Hadji Malick Diouf strongly linked, but it hardly seems a matter of urgency with Keane Lewis-Potter able to play as a wing-back with Rico Henry and Aaron Hickey also in the mix.

There is experienced striking cover in the shape of former England international Callum Wilson and an all-round depth to Keith Andrews' squad that was missing last season.

Do not expect it to be a hectic closing few days in the transfer window.

Another forward option - particularly down the left - would take this window for Brentford from a nine to a 10 out of 10.

Mykhailo Mudryk's name has been doing the rounds in recent weeks and Brentford have history there, having chased him prior to his move to Chelsea .

Get someone like Mudryk in, and I don't think the transfer window could've gone much better for Andrews.

It is anticipated Yankuba Minteh will leave for Liverpool , which might create space at Brighton for another forward and Carlos Baleba's exit for Manchester United may see the club make a move for midfield reinforcements.

It is possible there may be other exits but, as usual, Brighton will stick to their data driven recruitment plan.

"We must continue to evolve, invest and innovate while remaining true to the principles that have brought us this far," was chairman Tony Bloom's message to fans before the 4-0 win against Aston Villa .

With Baleba's anticipated departure and Minteh looking likely that he might leave as well, we need to bring a defensive midfielder who can bring a physical presence to our midfield and a winger who is proven at the top level.

We have a lot of games this season with European football, so we need to have the squad depth to compete on all fronts if we want to secure a top-10 finish again.

Chelsea supporters may want another star forward or a new goalkeeper to replace the unconvincing Robert Sanchez, but Xabi Alonso feels his squad is largely complete for this summer.

However, there is a huge amount of work to do to reduce the squad from 39 players to around 25 within the next eight days. That is the priority, as the Blues will not want frustrated players in their squad this season.

Chelsea need to focus more on the outgoings than incoming players.

With no Europe it's important we do not carry a squad that's too heavy, as we won't have too much room for rotation.

If we were to bring anybody in, I think the priority is a top-drawer goalkeeper.

Coventry are in the hunt for Mykhailo Mudryk as the Chelsea winger looks to get his career back on track after serving a 20 month suspension for testing positive for banned substance meldonium.

Defensive cover is also likely to be needed by Frank Lampard while players like Luke Woolfenden could leave on loan.

Honestly, I think we have done enough in the transfer window to build a team that can stay up in this league.

There has been a lot of change at Palace with the loss of Maxence Lacroix and a new manager starting the season in Pierre Sage.

The Eagles have been building depth for their Europa League campaign but still need a few bodies in the building.

Sage has made clear he wants a senior centre-back and Palace could be pushed to sign another defender too after the injury to Chadi Riad in the first game of the Premier League season against Everton .

Riad's injury has amplified the need for another centre-back who is first-team ready.

Axel Disasi is a good start, but a bigger, permanent move would be great. That, plus a central midfielder, and we are set.

Mateta's contract claim leaves Palace with transfer decision Published 1 day ago

Mateta's contract claim leaves Palace with transfer decision

Everton simply must sign a recognised right-back before the window shuts. It has been a glaring problem for more than a year.

It is a weakness recognised by everyone at the club but either a prime target cannot be agreed upon or is out of reach.

Talented midfielder Merlin Rohl took on the job for the opening game against Crystal Palace, while Jake O'Brien and James Garner have also been pressed into service.

Time to finally make a decision and get one in. Maybe David Moyes will also look at adding another striker with questions still hanging over Beto and Thierno Barry.

Chelsea outcast Liam Delap is one name regularly linked with Everton .

Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa has been clear that he is happy with the club's business so far, but more could be done to make his squad more balanced.

There have been attempts to sign an additional central defender, with a move for Rennes' Abdelhamid Ait Boudlal explored two weeks ago, and that could be a key area the Cottagers look to strengthen.

This is a club that does not operate at the very top end of the transfer market and one that enjoys a deadline-day deal.

It still feels like Fulham need a right winger - whether that is sticking with Oscar Bobb or providing serious competition for him - I think we need to cover for the loss of Harry Wilson's goals.

We also need a right-sided centre-back as there are serious concerns over how Joachim Anderson will fit Arbeloa's new system.

It has already been a busy summer for Hull City 's recruitment team but the ambitious Tigers are still working on adding two new forwards in Mohamed Ali-Cho and Ilyas Ansah.

There has also been interest from the club in Real Betis winger Pablo Garcia, although that deal has taken longer than hoped after the La Liga side raised their valuation of the 20-year-old. Stoke City's Sorba Thomas is also a player of interest.

A goalkeeper, midfielder and right-back also could be on the agenda for Sergej Jakirovic's side in the final week of the window.

Over the next week, if we bring in a left winger, one more striker - assuming the Ali-Cho deal also gets completed - a central midfielder, an attacking midfielder and a right-back to add depth and challenge Lewie Coyle for the starting spot, we will be in a strong position to compete.

Ipswich have spent over Â£150m on 12 new signings since returning to the Premier League.

Boss Gary O'Neil expects more, though, and a striker and a midfielder could arrive at Portman Road.

Fringe players like Anis Memeti could leave as O'Neil shapes his squad.

Having pushed the boat out to sign James Trafford from Manchester City , big money signings are probably off the agenda for Leeds in the last week of the window.

They are interested in taking Mykhailo Mudryk on loan but have not been able to strike a deal with the London club as yet as they are looking at other left wingers.

Leeds are also considering back-up options for forwards Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Lukas Nmecha and have also been linked with Frankfurt goalkeeper Michael Zetterer, if Lucas Perri joins Torino on loan as expected.

Leeds have had a great transfer window but they badly need another left-footed left-back as cover for Gabriel Gudmundsson.

Beyond that, perhaps another forward or creative midfielder to contend with Harry Wilson, Brenden Aaronson and Noah Okafor.

As has been the case for most of the summer, Liverpool 's priority remains the wide attacking areas and the expectation is that at least one and maybe two wingers will come in over the coming week.

Andoni Iraola said that personnel was not the issue when it came to defensive midfielders, the manner in which his side conceded twice at Newcastle would suggest that it would be wise to address Liverpool 's deficiencies in that department.

paragraphs: The first weekend of the Premier League season is complete but clubs still have one week of the transfer window remaining to secure last-minute squad additions.

Results are one thing but for many managers and sporting directors their opening match was an eye-opener in what positions need to be strengthened, who is no longer needed and what gaps still need to be plugged.
With the transfer window closing on Tuesday, 1 September at 23:00 BST, BBC Sport takes a look at what each top-flight club still needs and fans also have their say.
The Premier League champions have already strengthened the middle of the pitch with Bruno Guimaraes, the wing with Christos Tzolis and their defence with Ezri Konsa.
But Arsenal are still in the market for a forward and have a long-standing interest in Julian Alvarez.
Although it appears to be a difficult deal due to many factors, the Gunners will be ready to act if there is a chance to get it done.

If you want someone who is Premier League proven, who has won it all from the World Cup to the Champions League, Julian Alvarez looks like the guy that can take Arsenal to the promised land of finally getting over the line in Europe. Especially when there aren't that many elite forwards in the world.
Alvarez's Arsenal dilemma amid summer's most bitter transfer tussle Published 1 day ago
Alvarez's Arsenal dilemma amid summer's most bitter transfer tussle
Al-Hilal open talks to sign Arsenal winger Martinelli Published 1 day ago
Al-Hilal open talks to sign Arsenal winger Martinelli
What don't Aston Villa need after a raft of star departures this summer?
Ollie Watkins' transfer saga, with Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal trying to sign the striker, leaves Villa looking for a likely replacement with Nicolas Jackson a target.

A winger is also on the agenda while they need a defender after Ezri Konsa's move to Arsenal , and have opened talks for Club Brugge central defender Joel Ordonez after bids for Southampton centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis were rejected.
It is clear Aston Villa desperately require a striker more than anything right now.
Although I massively rate Victor Lindelof and Pau Torres, the display against Brighton has worried me slightly.
Therefore, I would welcome another centre-back as well.
It looks like we will be OK in midfield once Johan Manzambi is fit and with the addition of Leon Goretzka.

Villa in talks with Club Brugge for defender Ordonez
Bournemouth are used to being picked off and will simply be hoping to come through the final eight days of the transfer window unscathed.
It is clear that big clubs are circling for forward Eli Junior Kroupi and midfielder Alex Scott, who the Cherries insist are not for sale.
In terms of incomings, Bournemouth are largely done as they close in on a move for Juventus goalkeeper Michele Di Gregorio.
Brentford are in the fortunate position of being able to choose their deals carefully after some excellent squad strengthening.

The Bees have been looking at left-back, with West Ham's El Hadji Malick Diouf strongly linked, but it hardly seems a matter of urgency with Keane Lewis-Potter able to play as a wing-back with Rico Henry and Aaron Hickey also in the mix.
There is experienced striking cover in the shape of former England international Callum Wilson and an all-round depth to Keith Andrews' squad that was missing last season.
Do not expect it to be a hectic closing few days in the transfer window.
Another forward option - particularly down the left - would take this window for Brentford from a nine to a 10 out of 10.
Mykhailo Mudryk's name has been doing the rounds in recent weeks and Brentford have history there, having chased him prior to his move to Chelsea .
Get someone like Mudryk in, and I don't think the transfer window could've gone much better for Andrews.

It is anticipated Yankuba Minteh will leave for Liverpool , which might create space at Brighton for another forward and Carlos Baleba's exit for Manchester United may see the club make a move for midfield reinforcements.
It is possible there may be other exits but, as usual, Brighton will stick to their data driven recruitment plan.

"We must continue to evolve, invest and innovate while remaining true to the principles that have brought us this far," was chairman Tony Bloom's message to fans before the 4-0 win against Aston Villa .

With Baleba's anticipated departure and Minteh looking likely that he might leave as well, we need to bring a defensive midfielder who can bring a physical presence to our midfield and a winger who is proven at the top level.
We have a lot of games this season with European football, so we need to have the squad depth to compete on all fronts if we want to secure a top-10 finish again.
Chelsea supporters may want another star forward or a new goalkeeper to replace the unconvincing Robert Sanchez, but Xabi Alonso feels his squad is largely complete for this summer.

However, there is a huge amount of work to do to reduce the squad from 39 players to around 25 within the next eight days. That is the priority, as the Blues will not want frustrated players in their squad this season.
Chelsea need to focus more on the outgoings than incoming players.
With no Europe it's important we do not carry a squad that's too heavy, as we won't have too much room for rotation.
If we were to bring anybody in, I think the priority is a top-drawer goalkeeper.
Coventry are in the hunt for Mykhailo Mudryk as the Chelsea winger looks to get his career back on track after serving a 20 month suspension for testing positive for banned substance meldonium.
Defensive cover is also likely to be needed by Frank Lampard while players like Luke Woolfenden could leave on loan.
Honestly, I think we have done enough in the transfer window to build a team that can stay up in this league.
There has been a lot of change at Palace with the loss of Maxence Lacroix and a new manager starting the season in Pierre Sage.
The Eagles have been building depth for their Europa League campaign but still need a few bodies in the building.

Riad's injury has amplified the need for another centre-back who is first-team ready.
Axel Disasi is a good start, but a bigger, permanent move would be great. That, plus a central midfielder, and we are set.

articles.title: Sancris vuelve a casa para reforzar el ataque del Lega... desde Getafe
articles.standfirst: El atacante llega cedido por el club azulón con una opción de compra condicionada
articles.summary: El atacante llega cedido por el Getafe con una opción de compra condicionada
articles.body: Álex Sancris ya es nuevo jugador del Leganés. El conjunto pepinero ha alcanzado un acuerdo con el Getafe para la cesión por una temporada del atacante madrileño, de 29 años. La operación incluye además una opción de compra condicionada al término del curso. Su llegada supone el regreso a una casa que conoce perfectamente. Sancris militó durante cuatro temporadas en el filial pepinero, al que llegó en 2018 procedente del Trival Valderas. Fue capitán, logró el ascenso a Segunda Federación y en su última campaña firmó 10 goles antes de abandonar el club en 2022. Después pasó por el Linares y dio el salto al fútbol profesional con el Burgos, donde sus dos buenas temporadas le abrieron las puertas del Getafe. Ahora regresa a Butarque para ponerse a las órdenes de Rubén Albés y reforzar un ataque en el que ya están Unax del Cura, Gothler y Álex Millán. El fichaje tiene también un componente personal. Sancris volverá a compartir vestuario con Miguel Atienza, con quien mantiene una buena amistad después de coincidir durante su etapa en el Burgos. Sancris se marcha así al club en el que también jugó en categorías inferiores, al igual que pasó en Getafe. Tras una temporada con pocos minutos, Bordalás dejó claro que no contaba con el futbolista, que este curso no ha disputado minutos ni siquiera en pretemporada, donde no ha estado ni siquiera convocado. Pese a ello, en el Getafe siguen pensando que Sancris es un jugador que puede aportar en un futuro, por lo que el conjunto pepinero sólo tendrá esa opción de compra en caso de ascenso. Con ello, el Getafe sigue acelerando la operación salida a falta aún de que se ejecute en otros jugadores como Berrocal, Javi Muñoz y Neyou.
